data.title: Obfuscated Code and Control Flow
data.summary: Strings, control flow or both are deliberately obscured in the shipped binary or script — encoded strings decoded at runtime, opaque predicates, junk instructions — to slow static review without necessarily packing the whole file.
data.description:
Unlike packing, obfuscation of this kind leaves the file's overall structure intact and
operates at a finer grain: a string table that decodes itself with a one-byte XOR loop at
startup, control flow flattened into a single dispatcher with a state variable, or dead
branches inserted purely to inflate a disassembler's work. The intent is the same —
increase analyst time per sample — but the mechanism does not require an unpacking step.
data.recommendation:
* Decode obfuscated strings programmatically (identify the routine, re-run it standalone against the encoded blob) rather than by hand.
* Where control flow is flattened, trace the dispatcher's state variable through one execution to recover the logical order before reading the disassembly linearly.
* Keep the deobfuscation script; it is almost always reusable, unmodified, across the rest of the family.
data.short_recommendation: Automate string and control-flow deobfuscation rather than reviewing it by hand.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Strings decoded themselves via a single-byte XOR loop executed at module start.

mbc_techniques.implementation: String table stored XOR-encoded and decoded in place before first use.
